question: Should OpenClaw publish these three host-neutral recovery lifecycle sidecars as normative RFC 0013 follow-on contracts, including OpenClaw-owned restored admission and host-owned handoff orchestration?
rationale: The patch is documentation-only and contains no discrete implementation defect, but it proposes durable public ownership boundaries that determine future runtime and host compatibility obligations.

options.title: Keep as a separately sponsored follow-on
options.body: Retain the sidecars as a distinct draft direction until maintainers explicitly approve the ownership split and relationship to the base RFC.

options.title: Narrow to non-normative design notes
options.body: Move the material out of the completed RFC contract and retain it only as exploratory implementation guidance.

options.title: Reject the lifecycle contract direction
options.body: Keep RFC 0013 limited to single-database artifacts and leave aggregate handoff semantics to host-specific integrations.

recommendation.title: Keep as a separately sponsored follow-on
recommendation.body: Retain the sidecars as a distinct draft direction until maintainers explicitly approve the ownership split and relationship to the base RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal explicitly depends on the existing Gateway suspension boundary and asks this adjacent contributor to review the ownership split.
